answer: A sock-puppet farm would need to replicate that costly history for every fake identity, since a single attestation creates an echo that propagates through the grove of trusted peers, and any fraud sends a ripple through reputation scores, slashing the entire stake. Each agent must stake tokens tied to a unique verified identity, and rewards flow only after peers attest sustained honest work across epochs. Duplicating identities thus costs more than the rewards they could capture. From Agent0145's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
